question: Which of the following is NOT one of the off-road basic control skills test exercises listed in the manual?
choice_a: Highway merging at speed
choice_b: Straight line backing
choice_c: Forward through offset alley
choice_d: Alley dock
explanation: The manual lists straight line backing, forward through offset alley, parallel park (conventional), and alley dock as the off-road exercises; highway merging is not part of the off-road skills test.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Section 12 Introduction

question: The basic control skills test scoring is based on which of the following categories?
choice_a: Speed, fuel efficiency, and passenger comfort
choice_b: Encroachments, pull-ups, vehicle exits (looks), and final position
choice_c: Passenger comfort ratings only
choice_d: Total time taken and number of gear changes
explanation: The manual states the skills test is scored based on encroachments (crossing boundaries), pull-ups, outside vehicle observations (looks), and final position.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, 12.1 Scoring

question: What happens when an applicant strikes a cone or crosses an exercise boundary line during the skills test?
choice_a: The applicant receives only a verbal warning with no attempt used
choice_b: Nothing happens if it is judged a minor touch
choice_c: The test ends immediately with no further attempts allowed
choice_d: The examiner sounds a whistle, and it counts as an attempt
explanation: The manual states the examiner will sound a whistle for an encroachment, and each encroachment counts as an attempt, with remaining attempts starting from the originating position.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, 12.1 Scoring, Encroachments

question: What is a "pull-up" during the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Any gear change made during a maneuver
choice_b: When a driver stops and reverses direction to get a better position
choice_c: Any time the vehicle stops moving
choice_d: When the driver exits the vehicle to check its position
explanation: The manual defines a pull-up as when a driver stops and reverses direction to get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, 12.1 Scoring, Pull-ups

question: How many pull-ups is an applicant allowed per attempt during the basic control skills test?
choice_a: Unlimited
choice_b: Two
choice_c: One
choice_d: None
explanation: The manual states the applicant will be allowed one pull-up for each attempt.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, 12.1 Scoring, Pull-ups

question: Before exiting the vehicle to check its external position (a "look") during the skills test, the driver must:
choice_a: Simply open the door and step out
choice_b: Place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s)
choice_c: Turn off the engine completely and remove the key
choice_d: Ask a fellow applicant to check for them
explanation: The manual requires the driver to place the vehicle in neutral and set the parking brake(s) before safely exiting to check the vehicle's external position.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, 12.1 Scoring, Outside Vehicle Observations (Looks)

question: When safely exiting the vehicle during a "look" in the skills test, the driver must face the vehicle and maintain:
choice_a: Two points of contact
choice_b: No contact is required once outside the vehicle
choice_c: Three points of contact with the vehicle at all times
choice_d: One point of contact
explanation: The manual requires the driver to exit safely by facing the vehicle and maintaining three points of contact at all times (or a firm grasp on the handrail when exiting a bus).
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, 12.1 Scoring, Outside Vehicle Observations (Looks)

question: What happens if an applicant does not maneuver the vehicle into the exact final position instructed by the examiner?
choice_a: The applicant is automatically given one more attempt
choice_b: The applicant will disqualify on the basic control skills test
choice_c: Nothing, as long as the vehicle is within the coned area
choice_d: A minor point deduction is applied
explanation: The manual states that if the vehicle is not maneuvered into its final position exactly as instructed, the applicant will disqualify on the basic control skills test.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, 12.1 Scoring, Final Position

question: How many attempts is an applicant allowed for the straight line backing exercise?
choice_a: One
choice_b: Two
choice_c: Unlimited
choice_d: Three
explanation: The manual states the operator will have three attempts to complete the straight line backing maneuver.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Maneuver #1 Straight Line Backing

question: How many attempts is an applicant allowed for the forward through offset alley exercise?
choice_a: Two
choice_b: Four
choice_c: One
choice_d: Three
explanation: The manual states the operator will be allowed two attempts to complete the forward through the offset alley maneuver.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Maneuver #2 Forward Through the Offset Alley

question: In the reverse offset/parallel parking exercise, what constitutes one "attempt"?
choice_a: Any single steering correction
choice_b: Only the backward movement into the space
choice_c: The full duration of the exercise regardless of movements
choice_d: A backup and a drive ahead
explanation: The manual defines an attempt in the reverse offset/parallel parking exercise as a backup and a drive ahead; the operator is allowed three attempts.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Maneuver #3 Reverse Offset/Parallel Parking

question: In the alley dock exercise, the applicant must stop with the rear of the vehicle squared and no more than how many inches from the platform?
choice_a: 24 inches
choice_b: 18 inches
choice_c: 6 inches
choice_d: 12 inches
explanation: The manual requires the operator to back into the alley and stop with the rear of the vehicle squared and no more than twelve inches from the platform.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Maneuver #4 Alley Dock

question: For a tractor-trailer combination performing the alley dock maneuver, what must the tractor do?
choice_a: Detach from the trailer before backing into the alley
choice_b: Angling is never required for any combination vehicle
choice_c: Remain perfectly straight in line with the trailer
choice_d: Be positioned at a sharp angle to allow traffic to pass on the narrow street
explanation: If the test vehicle is a tractor-trailer combination, the tractor must be angled to the trailer at a sharp angle to allow traffic to pass on the narrow street.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Maneuver #4 Alley Dock

question: Which vehicle type is specifically noted as NOT required to angle the tractor during the alley dock maneuver?
choice_a: Straight trucks pulling a converter dolly
choice_b: All combination vehicles must angle regardless of type
choice_c: Standard tractor-semitrailer combinations
choice_d: Dump truck-flatbed trailer units
explanation: The manual specifically states that dump truck-flatbed trailer units are not required to be angled during the alley dock maneuver.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Maneuver #4 Alley Dock

question: For passenger (bus) and school bus endorsements, which maneuver replaces the standard alley dock exercise?
choice_a: A bus turnaround
choice_b: An emergency stop maneuver
choice_c: A three-point turn
choice_d: A figure-eight maneuver
explanation: The manual states that the alley dock is not a representative maneuver for a bus, so maneuver #4 for passenger and school bus endorsements is a bus turnaround instead.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Maneuver #4 Bus Turnaround

question: The bus turnaround maneuver starts with the bus positioned:
choice_a: Already inside the coned turnaround area
choice_b: Facing oncoming traffic at the edge of the area
choice_c: In the right lane of a two-lane roadway, beyond the turnaround area, parallel to the roadway
choice_d: In reverse gear at the curb
explanation: The bus turnaround maneuver starts with the bus positioned in the right lane of a two-lane roadway, beyond the turnaround area, a reasonable distance from the edge of the roadway and parallel to it.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, Maneuver #4 Bus Turnaround

question: The off-street basic control skills test area is set up using how many cones, flags, and ropes?
choice_a: 20 cones, 20 flags, and 6 ropes
choice_b: 15 cones, 15 flags, and 5 ropes
choice_c: 10 cones, 10 flags, and 3 ropes
choice_d: 5 cones, 5 flags, and 1 rope
explanation: The manual states the off-street skills test area is designed using 10 cones, 10 flags, and 3 ropes to limit the available room for the maneuvers.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills, 12.2 Exercises

question: During the on-road driving test, the applicant must do all of the following EXCEPT:
choice_a: Wear a safety belt
choice_b: Complete the test without an accident or moving violation
choice_c: Exceed the posted speed limit to keep up with traffic flow
choice_d: Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws
explanation: The manual requires wearing a safety belt, obeying all traffic laws, and completing the test without an accident or moving violation; it never instructs exceeding the posted speed limit.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1 How You Will Be Tested

question: According to the manual, "unsafe coasting" occurs when the vehicle is out of gear for longer than:
choice_a: The length of the vehicle
choice_b: 5 seconds
choice_c: The vehicle is never considered to be coasting unsafely
choice_d: One full city block
explanation: The manual defines unsafe coasting as when the vehicle is out of gear (clutch depressed or gearshift in neutral) for more than the length of the vehicle.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: When stopping behind another vehicle before making a turn, the driver should stop where they can see:
choice_a: The license plate of the vehicle ahead
choice_b: The top of the vehicle ahead
choice_c: Only the taillights of the vehicle ahead
choice_d: The rear tires of the vehicle ahead touching the ground
explanation: The manual instructs stopping where the driver can see the rear tires of the vehicle ahead touching the ground, maintaining a safe gap.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.1 Turns

question: While stopped at an intersection during the road test, the manual states the vehicle must:
choice_a: Be placed in reverse to prevent rolling
choice_b: Have the parking brake released at all times while stopped
choice_c: Not roll forward or backward
choice_d: Roll forward slightly to show proper engagement
explanation: The manual requires that while stopped at an intersection, the vehicle must not roll forward or backward.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.2 Intersections

question: After coming to a stop during the stop/start road test maneuver, what should the driver do regarding turn signals and flashers?
choice_a: Turn off all lights completely, including hazard flashers
choice_b: Activate the left turn signal only
choice_c: Cancel the turn signal and activate the four-way emergency flashers
choice_d: Leave the right turn signal on and take no other action
explanation: Once stopped, the manual instructs the driver to cancel the turn signal, activate the four-way emergency flashers, apply the parking brake, and shift to neutral or park.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: When resuming from the stop/start maneuver, the driver should not turn the steering wheel:
choice_a: Before the vehicle begins to move
choice_b: At all during the entire maneuver
choice_c: After merging back into traffic
choice_d: While the parking brake is still set
explanation: The manual instructs the driver not to turn the wheel before the vehicle moves when resuming from the stop/start maneuver.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.6 Stop/Start

question: Before entering a curve, the manual advises the driver to:
choice_a: Accelerate to maintain momentum through the curve
choice_b: Shift to neutral and coast through the curve
choice_c: Reduce speed so further braking or shifting is not required in the curve
choice_d: Move to the leftmost lane before entering
explanation: The manual instructs reducing speed before entering a curve so that further braking or shifting is not required while in the curve.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.7 Curve

question: While any part of a commercial vehicle is in a railroad crossing, the driver must not:
choice_a: Keep both hands on the wheel
choice_b: Look and listen for approaching trains
choice_c: Maintain a steady speed across the crossing
choice_d: Stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes
explanation: The manual states drivers must not stop, change gears, pass another vehicle, or change lanes while any part of the vehicle is in a railroad crossing.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: During the on-road test, while crossing railroad tracks, the driver should keep:
choice_a: One foot resting on the clutch pedal continuously
choice_b: Only one hand on the wheel to prepare for shifting
choice_c: Hands off the wheel briefly to check the mirrors
choice_d: Hands on the steering wheel as the vehicle crosses the tracks
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to keep their hands on the steering wheel as the vehicle crosses the tracks.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.8 Railroad Crossing

question: After driving under an overpass during the road test, the examiner may ask the applicant to state:
choice_a: The posted clearance or height
choice_b: The color of the overpass structure
choice_c: The number of support columns
choice_d: The overpass's construction date
explanation: After driving under an overpass, the applicant may be asked to tell the examiner what the posted clearance or height was; after a bridge, the posted weight limit.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.9 Bridge/Overpass/Sign

question: For manual transmission vehicles, the manual states the driver should NOT:
choice_a: Double-clutch when shifting
choice_b: Use the clutch when starting the engine
choice_c: Always use the clutch to shift
choice_d: Ride the clutch to control speed or "pop" the clutch
explanation: The manual instructs drivers not to ride the clutch to control speed, coast with the clutch depressed, or "pop" the clutch.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.11 Clutch Usage

question: When completing a left turn on a multiple-lane road, the vehicle should finish the turn in which lane?
choice_a: Any legal lane on the roadway
choice_b: The center lane exclusively
choice_c: The far-right (curb) lane
choice_d: The lane directly to the right of the center line
explanation: The manual states the vehicle should finish a left turn in the lane directly to the right of the center line, and finish a right turn in the right-most (curb) lane.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.14 Lane Usage

question: According to the manual's driving behavior scoring guidance, when should turn signals be canceled?
choice_a: They should stay on until the next turn is made
choice_b: Only when instructed to do so by the examiner
choice_c: Upon completion of a turn or lane change
choice_d: Turn signals cancel automatically and require no driver action
explanation: The manual instructs drivers to cancel turn signals upon completion of a turn or lane change.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.17 Use of Turn Signals

question: When exiting an expressway during the road test, the driver must continue to decelerate and:
choice_a: Change lanes within the exit ramp for a better position
choice_b: Maintain adequate spacing between the vehicle and others within the lane markings of the exit lane
choice_c: Accelerate briefly to merge back into traffic first
choice_d: Shift into neutral to coast down the ramp
explanation: The manual states that once on the exit ramp, the driver must continue to decelerate within the lane markings and maintain adequate spacing between the vehicle and other vehicles.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 13, On-Road Driving, 13.1.5 Expressway
